newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World cuts 96/97 groundnut output forecast.
newsitem.headline: Oil World cuts 96/97 groundnut output forecast.

text.p: Global production of edible groundnuts in 1996/97 is forecast at 19.92 million tonnes, shelled, up by 150,000 tonnes from 95/96, the independent Oil World newsletter said.
The publication said it had lowered by 120,000 tonnes an output forecast for 96/97 made in early April.
It cited drought-induced crop losses in Argentina, a smaller Senegalese crop and forecasts of a lower United States groundnut crop later this year.
As an indication of the consumption trend, it said direct edible use in net importing countries in 96/97 was forecast at 1.05 million tonnes, up from 1.03 million in 95/96.

World exports of groundnuts could rise to 1.31 million tonnes in 96/97 from 1.29 million previously but this would depend on the ability of Argentina, China, Vietnam and India to offset export supply shortfalls in the U.S.
Prices of U.S. beans could rise sharply over the next four to six months amid tight domestic supplies.
End-season stocks of groundnut oil in 96/97 (Oct/Sept) were seen falling to 411,000 tonnes from 458,000 a year earlier.
Oil usage was put at 4.39 million tonnes and output at 4.33 million.
